lines: West Side Story. Romeo and Juliet, with finger snaps and switchblades.
In nineteen forty-nine, it began as East Side Story: a Catholic boy, a Jewish girl. It stalled.
In nineteen fifty-five, headlines about youth gangs gave it new life.
So it moved to the Upper West Side. Two gangs, the Jets and the Puerto Rican Sharks. Tony and Maria fall in love across the line.
Jerome Robbins directed and choreographed. Bernstein wrote the music, Laurents the book, and a young Stephen Sondheim the lyrics.
It opened on Broadway in nineteen fifty-seven, and ran seven hundred thirty-two performances.
At the Tonys, it lost Best Musical to The Music Man.
But the film won ten Oscars, including Best Picture. Rita Moreno, as Anita, became the first Latina actress to win one.
Sixty years later, Ariana DeBose won for the very same role.
Some stories don't stay on one side of town.
